screen: MONITOR. Quick Access page window 855 x 766 (read by runbook A; the main Steam window was read here; screen not changed).
setup: Plugin open, no game running. Steam link sent from the SharedJSContext page with SteamClient.URL.ExecuteSteamURL. Page read from the main 'Steam Big Picture Mode' page: the highlighted entry in Settings' left-hand list (class containing 'Selected') and the heading (the first line of text after the list's last entry, Developer). A small watcher I placed on that page logged every change of both every 200 ms, and I matched its log to the send times (2.5 s apart). Watcher and my variables removed afterwards (checked: no p89 names left on either page). Way 2 reset: before each Navigate, I opened the Developer page by link (the System page for the 'developer' name), so a failed Navigate shows as Developer, not as a leftover of the page before.

second_way_found.what_exists: window.DFL is an object on SharedJSContext. DFL.Navigation has: Navigate, NavigateBack, NavigateToAppProperties, NavigateToExternalWeb, NavigateToInvites, NavigateToChat, NavigateToLibraryTab, NavigateToLayoutPreview, NavigateToSteamWeb, OpenSideMenu, OpenQuickAccessMenu, OpenMainMenu, CloseSideMenus, OpenPowerMenu. Other window keys matching the search: navigation, navigator, SteamUIStore, DFL, __ROUTER_HOOK_INSTANCE.
second_way_found.call_used: window.DFL.Navigation.Navigate('/settings/<name>') with the same 24 names (lowercase). Page location after each call (SharedJSContext location.pathname) always read /routes/settings/<name>, even for names where the page did not change (controller showed System while the path said controller): so the router path is not proof the right page drew.

pressed: No controller presses for the 24 pages (script only). Controller presses later: one B press after the Wi-Fi row, and for step 4 five B presses (see side_effect and step4).

Rows: 'Enable Wi-Fi / Settings > Internet' and '* QAM > Wi-Fi (QAM > Quick Settings)'. I walked DOWN (deck_walkTo, one press at a time, reading focus after each) instead of UP: box, then Ask, then the Enable Wi-Fi row (2 presses). The ring was on the row 'Enable Wi-Fi Settings > Internet', visible 100 percent.

After B the page went back to Home (/routes/library/home). The box was empty with no card when the plugin was shown again (the plugin cleared it itself; I did not press the clear button).

expected: Each of the 24 names opens its own settings page (list entry and heading match the label). The card's Enable Wi-Fi row opens the Internet page.
verdict: PASS (way 1) for 22 of 24 names: system, security, notifications, display, power, audio, bluetooth, controller, keyboard, customization, accessibility, friends, downloads, cloud, ingame, family, storage, gamerecording, home, library, store, developer.
FAIL (way 1) for 2 of 24: internet and remoteplay each opened the System page.
Way 2 (DFL.Navigation.Navigate): 23 of 24 opened their own page, including internet and remoteplay; controller did not (System).
Names neither way could open: none. Only 'internet' has a working link spelling for way 1 ('network'); no way 1 spelling worked for remoteplay.
FAIL step 5: the card's Enable Wi-Fi row opened System, not Internet (it uses the failing link name 'internet').
side_effect: My 100-plus script opens left Steam's page history long. B walked back through System/Developer settings pages instead of reaching Home; I used one Navigate call to Home to restore it. A left-stick click (L3) woke the screensaver. No setting was changed.
